learning_outcomes.text: Students can understand and explain a company and its business elements by applying modern Enterprise Architecture approaches to utilize reference maps, allowing them to operate effectively in future digital enterprises.

Analyze and evaluate the digitalization maturity in manufacturing companies by knowing, classifying, and understanding the potential and limitations of best-in-class information architectures, methods, and essential technologies, in order to derive courses of action for the maturity development of digital companies and their business processes.

Model the horizontal and vertical integration of IT systems by representing process chains, IT architectures, and system landscapes and explaining their interrelationships, in order to actively shape digitalization in production companies.

Evaluate the effort and benefit of digital technologies in a concrete application case by simulating or comparing different digitalization scenarios, in order to make fact-based decisions for digitalization measures.

syllabus_topics: Changes in the orientation of manufacturing companies in the context of digitalization and disruption of business areas through digital business models
Horizontal and vertical integration as the basis of digitalization, business processes and business process modeling, process map and main processes in production companies
Fundamental IT basic technologies and modern Cloud Architectures
Classification of mechanical engineering technologies and methods into the process chains of digitalized companies
Fundamentals of smart product creation and production management
The importance of information architectures and information flow in manufacturing companies today and tomorrow
IT system development and IT system classes such as ERP, CPQ, PLM, ALM, CRM, MES, MOM, WHM, PIM, CAx… in production companies in the context of digitalization
Approaches to paperless and drawingless production
Digital tools for creating mechatronic concepts
Digital tools for early 3D layout planning
Digital tools for designing automated systems
Digital tools for visualizing products and factories (DMU)
Digital tools for modeling and simulating production and production machines
Backbone systems such as PLM systems, ERP systems, ALM systems, MES systems, Industry Cloud
assessment_rules: The form of examination (written module exam, oral exam, or evaluated coursework) will be determined by the lecturer at the beginning of the course.
